note: Multi-turn transcripts, graded on CANONICAL STATE. Every case names the failure it exists to catch. The adversarial block is the one that decides the experiment: a correct number in the wrong life is the failure no numeric check can see.

transcript.text: About how much does the household spend each month on essentials, excluding rent and housing debt?
About two and a half thousand.

expect.why: The deterministic scan reads this as 2. Accepting that writes a EUR 2 monthly spend.

transcript.text: And roughly how much is sitting in savings and current accounts?

expect.why: No unit, no cadence, no subject in the client's own words. Everything that makes 400 meaningful is in the question before it.

transcript.text: And what is the balance on the mortgage?
Three hundred and twenty thousand — sorry, I mean three hundred and forty thousand.

expect.why: Correcting yourself mid-sentence is ordinary speech. Only the figure that stands may be written.

transcript.text: Do you each have a pension, and roughly what are they worth?
Mine is a hundred and eighty grand and hers is ninety.

expect.why: Both numbers are real. Swapping them is a correct figure in the wrong person's plan, and no numeric check can see it.

transcript.text: Tell me about your pension.
My work pension is about a hundred and eighty thousand.
Thanks. Has that changed recently?
The work pension is up to about a hundred and ninety thousand now.

expect.why: ONE pension, updated. Creating a second silently doubles the retirement pot, and every figure in it is one the client really said.

transcript.text: Do you have any pensions?
I have an old one from a previous job worth about eighty thousand, and my current work pension is around a hundred and eighty thousand.

expect.why: The mirror of the case above. Collapsing two real pensions into one loses a holding the client has.

transcript.text: What debts does the household have?
Just the mortgage, three hundred and forty thousand.
Any other debts apart from the mortgage?
No, none.

expect.why: 'No others' closes the collection and leaves the mortgage in it. Reading it as 'no debts' erases a real EUR 340,000 liability.

transcript.text: What is your pension worth now?
About a hundred and eighty thousand. What would it look like if I had three hundred thousand in it by sixty?

expect.why: A figure inside a what-if is a scenario the client is exploring, not money they hold.

transcript.text: Tell me about your savings and any borrowing.
I have about twenty thousand put by and my mortgage is three hundred and forty thousand.

expect.why: Two facts in one breath. Recovering one and dropping the other means the client is asked again for something they already said.

transcript.text: Do you have any other pensions?
There's another one from an old job but I've no idea what it's worth.

expect.why: A holding that exists with no figure must not become a figure, and must not be silently dropped either. The value stays outstanding.

transcript.text: Roughly what is the pension worth?
Around one eighty.

expect.why: 180 or 180,000 changes the plan completely. An honest question costs one turn.

transcript.text: How much do you have saved?
Two thousand in the credit union plus the other three in the current account.

expect.why: A total the client did not say is not a figure they stated.

transcript.text: Whose pension is the hundred and eighty thousand?
Actually that one is my wife's, not mine.

expect.why: An owner correction with no figure restated. The write must move the holding, not create a second one.

transcript.text: And the UK pension?
That one's about ninety thousand pounds.

expect.why: Writing euro for pounds is the same error as a wrong number, with a nicer failure mode: the figure looks right.
